identity.title: Beaver Valley Power Station, Unit No. 2 Docket No. 50-412, License No. NPF-73 LER 2023-003-01

cause.proximate_text: The direct cause of the door being left open is station personnel did not adequately track ownership of the door over the multi-day evolution... personnel not following the procedure when they did not assume ownership over the position of the door and did not shut the door at the end of the work activity. Additionally, a specific procedure did not exist for opening and closing this door. The root cause is the organization did not have a clear and concise process for controlling ownership and responsibility for missile shield doors should they need to be opened temporarily.
cause.theme: loss of ownership/administrative control over a temporarily opened missile barrier door

nodes.display_name: First work group failed to close door after work activity (Apr 6-7, 2023)
nodes.description: Responsible work group completed task and did not close door as required by 1/2-ADM-2021; no closure reported to control room; no Narrative Log entry stating door was shut.

nodes.display_name: Narrative Log authorization not carried over to later shifts
nodes.description: The Narrative Log entry authorizing the door to be opened was not carried over to later shifts, contributing to loss of tracked ownership.

nodes.display_name: Second work group left door open (Apr 7, 2023)
nodes.description: Second work group found door already open, determined prior authorization existed and had not been closed, and left it open as found after completing their own work.

nodes.display_name: Responsibility and control of door position lost
nodes.description: Since the door was not closed by either work group and log entries were not carried over, responsibility for the door and control of its position were lost.

nodes.display_name: Door remained open through refueling outage and Mode transitions
nodes.description: Door A-35-5A remained open throughout 2R23 (from April 9, 2023) and Mode 4 was entered on May 14, 2023 with the door still open.

nodes.display_name: CCP System loss of safety function / both trains inoperable (tornado missile protection breach)
Add door A-35-5A closure check to daily operator tour logs
Create procedures for opening/closing doors A-35-5A and F-66-3
Add dedicated closure team requirement and additional door controls to 1/2-ADM-2021 for A-35-5A and F-66-3

nodes.title: Containment Equipment Hatch Missile Shield Removal Inadvertently Results in Exceeding Technical Specification 3.6.1 Required Completion Times
Inadequate Tornado Missile Protection Identified Due to Non-Conforming Design Conditions
Intake Structure Interconnecting Flood Door Found Open Resulting in a Loss of Train Separation for the Reactor Plant River Water System

chain: no clear ownership/control process for temporarily opened missile doors [cause TBD] -> work group fails to close door A-35-5A after task -> Narrative Log authorization not carried over -> second work group leaves door open as found -> responsibility/control of door lost -> door remains open through outage and Mode 4 entry -> CCP System loss of safety function, both trains inoperable (~35 hrs + ~27 days)
notes: This is Revision 01 correcting the inoperability window/dates and confirming completion of corrective actions from the original 2023-003-00 LER. Official cause code is TBD/provisional per FORM-366 fields even though narrative describes a clear direct/root cause (personnel/procedural ownership failure); category left as 'provisional' per rule 4. No equipment failure occurred; this is a purely administrative/procedural failure chain affecting a passive missile barrier and consequent CCP train inoperability. No backup system is stated as compensating for the loss of CCP safety function (the very-low-risk determination rests on PRA/tornado-missile probability analysis, not on an operable backup system), so no BACKED_UP_BY edge is asserted. ADS/HPCI not applicable to this PWR CCP event.
